title: Maturation of River‐Dominated Delta Tops: The Channelized Delta Model
content:
Abstract

We present a novel, laterally averaged model of delta growth, the channelized delta model, in which delta top dynamics are described in terms of channelized (lumped channel) and non-channelized areas. The maturation level of the lumped channel is defined by a shape factor that dictates flow partitioning between channelized and non-channelized areas. Mature channel geometry is determined with an empirical, bankfull Shields number closure. In other words, a mature channel can convey the formative (bankfull) discharge with sub-aerially exposed non-channelized areas. Juvenile channels are shallower, have higher cumulative width and a smaller conveyance capacity than mature channels. For this reason, non-channelized areas surrounding juvenile channels are submerged at formative flow. Juvenile channels mature as fine sediment deposits on non-channelized areas, increasing flow confinement. We validate the model on the Colorado River Delta into Lake Mead shortly after Hoover dam closure. Simulations of 100 years of delta growth show the downstream migration of the spatial transition from mature to juvenile channels. This transition represents an internal moving boundary indicating the visible extent of the delta at formative discharge. The submerged fraction of the delta top depends on the relative speed of shoreline advancement versus the mature-juvenile transition advancement. The formulation presented here can predict delta growth and local changes in channel geometry over 100s of years with limited computational costs and can be of aid in site-specific applications when limited field data is available.
